MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  NOVEMBER 25, 2024
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  5:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Stewart called the meeting to order at 4:30 pm.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne Riggins; and
  Councilmembers Paul Grisanti, Bruce Silverstein and Steve Uhring.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: None.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  At 4:31 p.m., the Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss the following items listed
  on the Closed Session agenda:

Conference with Legal Counsel — Anticipated Litigation

  l.  Initiation of litigation pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of Government
  Code section 54956.9
  Number of potential cases: (1)

Conference with Legal Counsel — Existing litigation pursuant to Government Code Section
54956.9(d)(1):

  1.  Case Name: City’s Petition to Form Malibu USD from Territory in the Santa
  Monica-Malibu USD

REGULAR SESSION CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Stewart called the meeting to order at 5:31 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne  Riggins;  and
  Councilmembers Paul Grisanti, Bruce Silverstein and Steve Uhring.

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Joseph Toney, Assistant City
  Manager; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin
  Riesgo, Community Services Director; Yolanda Bundy, Environmental Sustainability
  Director; Susan Duefias, Public Safety Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director;
  Parker Davis, Media Technician; Christina Munoz, Deputy City Clerk; Tracey Rossine,
  Environmental Programs Manager; Arthur Aladj adjian, Public Works Superintendent; and
  Travis Hart, Deputy Public Works Director

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Norm Haynie led the Pledge of Allegiance.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attorney Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 4:30 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.9 and 54956.9(d)(l), with all Councilmembers present. He stated the Council
  discussed the items on the Closed Session agenda and took no reportable action.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  November 13, 2024.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Councilmember Uhring moved, and Councilmember Silverstein seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda. The motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 1  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment. As there were no public
  speakers present for the Consent Calendar, the Mayor returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

  Item Nos. 1.B.8. and 1.B.10. were pulled by the Council.

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Uhring seconded a motion
  to approve the Consent Calendar, pulling Item Nos. 1.B.8. and 1.B.10. The motion
  carried unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.

  reading of ordinances considered on this agenda for introduction on first
  reading and/or second reading and adoption.
  Approve Warrants

  74190-74299 on the register from the General Fund and direct the City

  Recommended Action: 1) Accept the work performed by Toro Enterprises,

  Authorize the Public Works Director to submit for recordation a Notice of
  Completion.
  Acceptance of Trancas Canyon Park Upper and Lower Slopes Repair
  Project
  Recommended Action:  1) Accept the work performed by GMZ
  Engineering, Inc. for the Trancas Canyon Park Upper and Lower Slopes
  Repair Project, Specification No. 2092 as complete; and 2) Authorize the
  Public Works Director to submit for recordation a Notice of Completion.
  Acceptance of Legacy Park Benches Renovation Proiect
  Recommended Action: 1) Accept the work performed by Blackpointe
  Group Construction & Management, Inc. for the Legacy Park Benches
  Renovation Project, Specification No. 2105 as complete; and 2) Authorize
  the Public Works Director to submit for recordation a Notice of Completion.
11.  Award Las Flores Canyon Storm Drain Repair Proiect

  Recommended Action: 1) Approve the award of bid and authorize the
  Mayor to execute an agreement with J & H Engineering General
  Contractors, Inc. (J & H) in the amount of $80,075 for the construction of
  the Las Flores Canyon Storm Drain Repair Project, Specification No. 21 1 1;
  and 2) Authorize the Public Works Director to approve any potential change
  orders up to 20%.
  12.  Amendment to Professional Services with m6 Consulting. Inc.
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 1
  to the Professional Services Agreement with m6 Consulting, Inc. (m6) for
  engineering design services for disaster projects in an amount of $26,900
  for a total amount not to exceed $337,185 and extend the term of the
  agreement through July 12, 2026.
  13.  California Employer’s Retiree Benefit Trust Program
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 24-59 to update the
  Delegation of Authority to Request Disbursements for the California
  Employers’ Retiree Benefit Trust Program (CERBT) and rescind
  Resolution No. 09-27.
  14.  Professional Services Agreement with Kimlev Horn
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute a professional
  services agreement with Kimley Horn to develop a Speed Safety System
  Use Policy and Impact Report.
  15.  Investment Report for the Month Ending October 3 1 , 2024
  Recommended Action: Receive the Investment Report for the month
  ending October 31, 2024.
  16.  Reiection of Bids for the Latigo Canyon Retaining Walls Rehabilitation
  Project
  Recommended Action: 1) Reject all bids received for the Latigo Canyon
  Retaining Walls Rehabilitation Project, Specification 2087; and 2) Direct
  staff to readvertise for construction bidding after FEMA/ CalOES has
  authorized the additional funding.

  The following items were pulled from the consent calendar for individual consideration:

  8.  Acceptance of Trancas Canyon Park Playground Resurfacing Project
  Recommended Action: 1) Accept the work performed by Robertson
  Industries, Inc. for the Trancas Canyon Park Playground Resurfacing
  Project, Specification No. 2109 as complete; and 2) Authorize the Public
  Works Director to submit for recordation a Notice of Completion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, andCouncilmember Grisanti seconded a
  motion to 1) accept the work performed by Robertson Industries, Inc. for
  the Trancas Canyon Park Playground Resurfacing Project, Specification
  No. 2109 as complete; and 2) authorize the Public Works Director to submit
  for recordation a Notice of Completion. The mOtion carried unanimously.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of November 25, 2024
  Page 5 of 11

  10.  Professional Services Agreement for Bluffs Park Snack Shack
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute a Professional
  Services Agreement with Pacific Architecture and Engineering, Inc. (PAC)
  in an amount not to exceed $200,000 for engineering design services for the
  Bluffs Park Snack Shack project.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

CONENSUS  By consensus, the Council directed staff to include with the Subcommittee
  and Ad Hoc Committee appointment item in January 2025 an option to
  consider forming an ad hoc committee to address recreational use on all
  City properties and the development of the Malibu Bluffs Park snack shack.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a
  motion to authorize the Mayor to execute a Professional Services
  Agreement with Pacific Architecture and Engineering, Inc. (PAC) in an
  amount not to exceed $200,000 for engineering design services for the
  Bluffs Park Snack Shack proj ect. The motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 2  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  Paciflc Coast Highway Safety Update Presentation

  Deputy City Manager Brown presented an update on Pacific Coast Highway (PCH)
  safety proj ects, including speed camera implementation, plans for PCH
  roundabouts at El Matador State Beach and Encinal Canyon Road, and the Caltrans
  PCH Master Plan Feasibility Study.

  The Council directed questions to staff.

ITEM 3  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  Assistant City Manager Toney announced City Hall would be closed Thursday and
  Friday for Thanksgiving. He stated the next Regular meeting on December 9 would
  include the City Council reorganization and be followed by a reception in the Muli-
  purpose Room. He announced the next City Manager Update would be distributed
  on December 2, 2024 and encouraged the public to sign up for notifications.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, reported on
  October crime statistics and stated there were 380 part one crimes, which is down
  from last year. He discussed an incident on November 13, 2024 where the special
  assignment deputies assisted with 13 search warrants in Los Angeles County as part
  of an investigation into Mexican cartels. He discussed the warrant served in
  Woodland Hills and the total volume of narcotics and weapons retrieved. He
  discussed an incident where deputies responded to a physical altercation between
  squirrel trappers and parents at Malibu High School (MHS).
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of November 25, 2024
  Page 6 of 11

  Councilmember Grisanti discussed potential flnes from Fish and Game for
  relocating squirrels.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Sergeant Soderlund confirmed none of
  the search warrants were served in Malibu. He confirmed he could compare crime
  statistics to multiple past years and discussed trends over the last five years ago.
  He discussed “swatting” emails, and stated it was important to investigate them and
  treat them as real reports. He encouraged individuals to report those emails to the
  Sheriff s Department.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, Sergeant Soderlund stated California
  Highway Patrol and Sheriff’s Department officers could enforce the ban on trucks
  over three axels on PCH.

  RECESS  At 6:08 p.m., Mayor Stewart recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 6:30
  p.m. with all Councilmembers present.

  ITEM 4.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Guy discussed Councilmember Uhring’s comments at the last meeting and

Q}  questioned why Councilmember Uhring wanted to know the name of the person
  who reported his property to code enforcement. He discussed the cost of potential
  litigation related to Councilmember Uhring and Councilmember Silverstein’s
  actions.

  Will Spano discussed the Malibu Township Council and stated it tried to control
  the City. He discussed Councilmember Uhring’s previous role as President of the
  Malibu Township Council. He discussed Malibu Township Council members on
  City Commissions and their activity on Nextdoor.

  ITEM 4.B.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Uhring stated he attended the last Library Speaker Series event and
  discussed how the program brought the community together. He commended
  Community Services Director Riesgo and Los Angeles County Community Library
  Manager Stallings for their work on the events. He discussed cell service outages
  during public safety power shutoff (PSPS) events. He discussed the item coming
  back in January to consider forming a body to address issues related to PSPS events.
  He encouraged the community to look out for their neighbors during PSPS. He
  discussed Waste Management increasing rates and encouraged seniors to apply for
  the 10% senior discount. He discussed City Council Policy #43 and how it was
  being interpreted by staff. He discussed the General Municipal Election and the
  election results. He discussed Hans Laetz’s recent comments on Nextdoor.

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins stated she introduced the speaker at the last Library
  Speaker Series event, and commended Community Services Director Riesgo and
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes 0f Novemb€r 25, 2024
  Page 7 of 11

  Los Angeles County Community Library Manager Stallings for their work on the
  events. She stated she attended the Los Angeles County Office of Education Board
  of Education (LACOE) hearing at MHS on the City’s petition to form the Malibu
  Unified School District. She stated she attended the ribbon cutting in Westlake
  Village for its new pickleball court and suggested using their recreation center as a
  model. She stated she attended the Los Angeles County Library Commission
  meeting. She stated she attended a Parks and Recreation Commission meeting
  where the Equestrian Park was discussed. She suggested conducting a flashvote
  survey targeted toward use of the Equestrain Park.

  Assistant City Manager Toney requested the Council direct staff to bring back an
  item if they would like to consider doing a survey.

  In response to Mayor Stewart, Mayor Pro Tem Riggins stated Trancas Riders and
  Ropers was still active. Community Services Director Riesgo stated Trancas Riders
  and Ropers recently contact City staff and intend to start using the facility again.
  She stated the group was working on new programs and would contact the City
  again in January.

  In response to Councilmember Grisanti, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated the City did not pay fees for the use of the Equestrian Park but did pay for
  maintenance.

  Mayor Stewart proposed bringing back update in January.

  Councilmember Silverstein indicated support for the item Mayor Pro Tem Riggins
  requested.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, Assistant City Manager Toney confirmed
  that staff could bring back an update.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an update on Equestrian Park
  use and options for possible outreach.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, Public Safety Director Dueflas stated she
  could look into adding the evacuation zone numbers to the beacon boxes around th
  City.

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins discussed Councilmember Uhring’s comments on the
  election and stated she was not pro-development. She discussed her philosophy
  when considering development applications.

  Councilmember Silverstein stated he had been preparing a list of proposals he
  hoped the City Council could consider over the next year. He stated he had been
  working with Councilmember-elect Haylynn Conrad on an item regarding a
  dedicated senior center. He discussed the need to improve the City’s evacuation
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes ofNovember 25, 2024
  Page 8 of 11

  plan. He discussed allowing individuals on Zoom in public meetings to be on
  camera. He discussed his proposal to limit remote participation in hybrid meetings
  to residents. He discussed requiring remote participants to sign up to speak in
  advance. He discussed City Council Policy #43. He stated remote participants and
  Hans Laetz continue to spread misinformation. He discussed Jo Drummond’s
  residency in the City and his intent to appoint her to the Flaming Commission. He
  stated he was not a member of the Malibu Township Council, but he appreciated
  the work they do. He discussed the City Council’s decision to prohibit league play
  at Trancas Park. He discussed Hans Laetz’s blog and reporting. He discussed
  different Views on the environment and property rights among the
  Councilmembers.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated there
  was a condition on the approval for Trancas Canyon Park prohibiting league play
  and there was a provision in the settlement agreement with Malibu Township
  Council that the City would not change that condition.

  Councilmember Grisanti discussed Councilmember Uhring’s comments and the
  restrictions on league play at Trancas Canyon Park. He encouraged the public to
  participate in the upcoming Community Emergency Response Team (CERT)
  training course. He stated he attended a Las Virgenes-Malibu Council of
  Governments (COG) meeting with Mayor Stewart. He stated he attended the
  LACOE hearing at MHS. He discussed the emails sent to the residents attacking
  him during the election.

  Mayor Stewart stated he attended the LACOE hearing at MHS. He stated he
  attended and Administration and Finance Subcommittee meeting. He discussed
  hind reserves and the costs of developing and maintaining the City’s community
  lands. He commended the Library Speaker Series organizers. He discussed the
  item coming back to form a group to address PSPS events. He discussed the 20
  years it took to build the recreation facilities in Westlake Village and the challenges
  they faced. He discussed plans for roundabouts on PCH. He discussed the COG’S
  plans for using excess capacity in flberoptic systems being installed throughout the
  COG. He discussed the recognition of Councilmember Grisanti leaving office at
  the COG meeting. He requested an update from Building Safety on soft structures
  in the City.

  In response to Mayor Stewart, Environmental Sustainability Director Bundy stated
  the City had completed the first phase of the soft story retrofit proj ect. She
  discussed plans for the project. She stated there were 43 sites being monitored by
  staff for potential landslides and discussed mediation steps being taken.

  Mayor Stewart discussed the recently adopted Code of Conduct for elected and
  appointed officials. He discussed misinformation spread from inside and outside
  the city.

ITEM 5  ORDINANCES AND PUBLIC HEARINGS

  None.

  ITEM 7  NEW BUSINESS

  Malibu LibrarV Set Aside Funds for Fiscal Year (FY) 2025-26
  Recommended Action: Approve Prioritized Funding List for FY 2025-26 as
  recommended by the Library Subcommittee.

  Deputy City Manager Brown presented the staff report.

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment. As there were no speakers
  present, Mayor Stewart returned the matter to the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

  MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion
  to approve the Prioritized Funding List for FY 2025-26 as recommended by the
  Library Subcommittee. The motion carried unanimously.

  Bonsall Drive and Busch Drive Speed Humps Request
  Recommended Action: 1) Install speed humps on Bonsall Drive between Pacific
  Coast Highway to end Bonsall Drive, and Busch Drive between Harvester Road
  and Cuthbert Road; and 2) Direct staff to present the proposed project to
  Administrative & Finance Subcommittee seeking additional funding for the
  placement of rubberized molded speed humps during the current flscal year.

  Public Works Director DuBoux presented the staff report.

  The Council directed questions to staff.

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: Quentin Lilly, Tiffany Murray, Jonathan Mone, Brian Spun, John Ferry

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Stewart returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

U
  MOTION  Councilmember Grisanti moved, and Councilmember Silverstein seconded a
  motion to: 1) approve installing speed humps on Bonsall Drive between Pacific
  Coast Highway to end Bonsall Drive, and Busch Drive between Harvester Road
  and Cuthbert Road; and 2) direct staff to present the proposed project to
  Administrative & Finance Subcommittee seeking additional funding for the
   Malibu City Council

  placement of rubberized molded speed humps during the current fiscal year.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Councilmember Silverstein moved to approve $100,000 spending up to $100,000
  on the purchase of rubberized molded speed humps.

  The maker of the motion accepted the amendment.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

  The motion carried unanimously.

  Community Development Department Organizational Plan
  Recommended Action: 1) Receive and file the Community Development
  Department organizational plan; 2) Approve the creation of the Community
  Development Director position; and 3) Adopt Resolution No. 24—60 amending the
  Salary Ranges, Authorized Positions, and Class Descriptions for FY 2024-25.

  Assistant City Manager Toney presented the staff report.

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: Jo Drummond, Will Spano

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Stewart returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved to: 1) receive and f11e the Community
  Development Department organizational plan; 2) approve the creation of the
  Community Development Director position; and 3) adopt Resolution No. 24—60, as
  amended to: a) become effective upon the start date of a new Community
  Development Director, b) add the at the beginning of the physical'demands section
  of each class specification “subject to any reasonable accommodation that is
  required by the American with Disabilities Act or California Disabled Persons
  Act”, c) remove the word “customer” from the class specifications, and d) add to
  the Community Development Director, Assistant Community Development
  Director, and Planning Manager Class Specifications “shall strive to obtain
  certification from AICP”, amending the Salary Ranges, Authorized Positions, and
  Class Descriptions for FY 2024—25.

  The Council discussed the motion.

  Mayor Stewart seconded the motion.
   Malibu City Council

  The question was called and the motion carried 3-1-1, Mayor Pro Tern Riggins
  opposed and Councilmember Grisanti abstained.

  None.

  Mayor Stewart adj ourned the meeting at 9: 10 p.m.
